chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Hamzah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about collateral and guarantee in credit sales, and he said, 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.الرُّهُونِ: Collateral or pledge given to secure a debt
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is collateral allowed in credit sales according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) validates the use of collateral (*rahn*) and guarantee (*takfil*) in credit sales (*bai' al-nasi'ah*), affirming their compatibility with Islamic commercial law. This ruling provides essential legal clarity for merchants, ensuring that securing debt through these mechanisms does not void the underlying contract, a principle widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence.
